name: SPX JEV question set, final (round 3: audits applied)
built_from: round 3: audit of 10-questions-final.json (scratchpad/audit10), data-truth check (scratchpad/dtcheck), defects check (scratchpad/chk11); fixes in scratchpad/final10/patch12.py; checks in scratchpad/fix12/chk.py
owner_rule: A question goes to shadow only once proven not to help JEV's direction call; unproven questions stay live and the learning loop's weights sort them out.

conventions.status: live = asked on its cadence and a candidate for the combiner weights from day one (every question not proven useless, by the owner's rule; the learning loop's weights sort them out). shadow = asked, logged and graded but kept out of the weights, used ONLY where there is proof the question does not help the direction call (each carries shadow_proof). dark = never asked because a feed or data is missing on Monday. A question that waits only on a build (a writer, a scan field) stays dark inside its home group; the dark group holds the feed-missing ones. Retired questions leave the set and are listed under 'retired'.
conventions.availability_vs_status: label availability is separate: live labels are on the row/bars today; cheap_add labels need a Schwab series saved or a small builder/calendar change (all fetchable; build before Monday or the question sleeps with its label omitted); dark labels need a new feed.
conventions.placeholders: No number is written in instructions, option descriptions or criteria: every threshold is a {lower_case} name filled from spx_jev/cuts.py QUESTION_CONSTANTS (names match cuts.json where a measured cut exists; new names must be added to cuts.py, flagged in_cuts_py=false). Tokens 0DTE, 1DTE, S&P 500, Nasdaq-100, 0-to-7-day, 1-to-7-day, VIX9D, VIX3M, VIX1D are names, not numbers. Label example sentences carry the figure AND the rule it was judged against, so JEV never compares numbers.
conventions.gamma_words: No label or option says long/short gamma, dealer hedging, damp, calm or pin for the sign. The book is described as the call-vs-put gamma balance at price 'under the usual assumption that dealers hold the calls and are short the puts'; the flip is a price level. Code learns the mapping (regime equals price's side of the flip on 2460/2462 rows).
conventions.sign_free_crosses: Questions that cross a second signal with the move say agree / against / quiet, not up/down (price_move_5way is the one carrier of the move's sign). ref_side names the reference the learning loop should fold on.
conventions.gating: A question whose default answer would be 'nothing happened' (no touch, no shock, not pinned, no release, too early) is asleep in code instead of carrying that option, so the default never enters the weights.
conventions.rulers: Distances and moves in sigma_anchor (anchor guard; row.sigma ratchet removed from grader and labeller). Size by same-clock rank or the tape unit, never a fixed sigma cut. The straddle only inside straddle questions. Normal-day sigma (20-session median anchor) only for events. VIX points, basis points, TICK and shares keep their native units; no raw index points in sentences. Every size or judgement of a market measure is its rank against the same measure at the same clock on up to the last 20 prior sessions (night_rank_count), at least 10 usable (same_clock_min_sessions), said by its third (or fifth where the options need one) in plain words; a measure in sigma skips 'ruler estimated' days, one in its native units keeps every session; under the minimum the label is omitted with the reason, never judged on a fixed line. Fixed numbers stay only as definitions: window lengths, clock times, lookback and minimum counts, rank band edges, giveback shares that define a word, touch tolerances, unit conversions and freshness limits. A premarket read sizes in the pre-open ruler, the median morning anchor of the last sessions (rulers.normal_day_sigma), stamped on its record; the night's measures are ranked in percent of price against the same measure on the last 20 nights (night_rank_count), at least 10 usable (overnight_rank_min_nights), skipping roll, holiday and short nights.
conventions.settled_open: close of the 09:34 bar, never the 09:30 print (median 0.115 sigma stale; 28% of a real gap made after 09:30).
conventions.cadence: The live lane reads at :02 and :32 only (cadence.py); '30-minute read' means those. The opening lane reads every 5 minutes 09:35-10:30. The premarket lane saves the overnight futures and builds every label at six checkpoints before the open (02:35, 03:35, 08:05, 08:48, 09:05 and 09:28 ET; 03:35 moves to 04:35 in the week Frankfurt is on winter time and New York is not) and asks JEV only at the reads a question's schedule names (08:48 and 09:28); its answers are graded from the settled open, 10 and 30 minutes on, and are never held into the other lanes. A group request carries only its awake questions, so one group can serve both session lanes. Day constants are asked once and held.
conventions.reading_checks: code_answer=true means the builder can compute the correct option from the same numbers the labeller used; it is stored beside every request (not sent) and JEV's pick is scored against it each read at no extra call (extends SNDK ab_test.py to multi-label questions). Offline nightly probes on archived scenes: mirror (swap direction words; code-answer questions must flip exactly), blind (drop the key label), mismatch (figure vs verdict words), decoy (irrelevant label), option-order reversal, and a gamma-word flip on the sum. Probes never feed the weights; a failing question gets reworded, not shadowed.
conventions.location_first: Labels and options state where price is now before any history (the SNDK back-inside fix, 3/12 -> 40/40).
conventions.thirty_minute_start: The 30-minute lane's first read (clock.FIRST_READ 09:32) comes before the 09:34 settled open; every 30-minute-lane question starts at 10:02 unless its schedule says later, and the 09:32 read is skipped.
conventions.schedule: Every question carries a machine schedule {lane: {every_min, from, to} or {at: [...]}} beside the free-text cadence (cadence.DOC_TEXT phrases like 'every other 30-minute read (hourly)' are not parsed by parse_cadence); code reads the schedule, never the text.
conventions.sleep_when: A gated question carries sleep_when: the code rule under which it is not asked (its default 'nothing happened' state), so that default never enters the weights.
conventions.horizon: horizon is a {lane: horizon} map on every multi-lane question; single-lane questions keep a plain string.
conventions.needs_engine_edit: needs_engine_edit marks engine labels (spec/labels.json) this set rewords. availability says whether the data is on the row; whether a label is built is the code's to say: a label no family writes is omitted as not built (labels/registry.py), and a question reading it is skipped as missing it.
conventions.score_criteria: type score: criteria is an ordered list, index = level, in the same order as options (spec 01).
conventions.tags: tags marks a kind of question across groups. SEQUENTIAL_READ: the label states two or more steps in time order and the answer depends on that order; a question's steps are rebuilt from bars at every read, never from JEV's earlier answers. Untagged questions carry no tags field.

daily_expiry_handling.summary: SPX lists an SPXW expiry every trading day. The question set treats today's 0DTE book as the dealer book of record, but corrects for what a daily expiry does.
rules: Morning book share: today's 0DTE book is only a median 32-34% of the 0-to-7-day book's gamma before noon, rising to 55% by 15:30. gamma_weight_both_books reads the week's book beside today's; book_balance_agreement names which book each clause reads.
Grip climbs all day as the settle nears (median top-strike share 6.3% at 10:30 to 9.6% at 15:45), so magnet_seat ranks grip against the same clock, never a fixed cut.

Speed limit, then magnet: the magnet does not pull price before 15:00 (distance vs next 30 min -0.23 at 14:02); after 15:30 it does, through the 15:50 auction (+0.41). magnet_seat is a size question all day; settle_pull_side is the direction question at 14:02-15:32 with per-slot weights.
Shrinking ruler: distance to the pin is also stated in remaining straddles (range_ruler.em_points), because the same 0.2 sigma is out of reach at 13:30 and inside the priced move at 15:30.

0DTE last hour: at-the-money IV moves a median 2.07 vol points per 30 minutes in the last hour vs 0.82 earlier (cuts.json), an expiry-clock effect; atm_iv_vs_price's beta and bands must be refit or suppressed in the last hour (ZERO_DTE_LAST_HOUR_MIN 60).

Engine wording: expiry.settle_clock's 'gamma decays fastest' reads as 'pin releasing' to JEV; near-the-money weight actually concentrates into the settle. Reworded before Monday. expiry.today_vs_week loses its 'damps/feeds moves' clause.

Settlement types: the monthly (third Friday) SPX book is morning-settled on the opening prints, so its gamma is gone after 09:30 while daily SPXW still settle at 16:00; the quarter-end SPXW book is close-settled and holds the hedged-equity collar. expiry_calendar separates them; the 09:34 settled-open convention already moves past the special opening quotation (opex 09:35-09:39 ranges at the 3rd-17th percentile).

Quarter-end 09-30: dated_gex/book.json drops the expiring quarter-end band in every September pull, so quarter_end_collar_side is dark until the band filter is fixed; the 0-to-7-day ladder shows the weight only blended.

Hand-off: the 0DTE and week books disagree on sign on 15-24% of reads before noon but only 7-10% after 15:00, so the hand-off largely happens overnight; no 1DTE slice is needed for the close questions. A tomorrow-book question is dark (needs a 1DTE scan slice) and contested.
Big-book days: Friday 0DTE open interest is about 1.7x other days but does not predict the rest-of-day range (Spearman 0.00, n=40); no weekday or book-size question.

Monthly-expiry days on file were quiet (range 0.45-0.55 sigma vs 0.60) and 2 of 3 days after were wide; expiry_calendar serves size. Test window: 09-30 quarter-end, 10-12..10-16 opex week, 10-16 monthly, 10-19..10-23 after.
Half days close at 13:00 (sessions.py); settle clocks and session progress use the real close.
Grading: settle and pin questions are graded on the official close, which differs from the 15:59 bar by up to 0.06 sigma (09-18 quad witching +4.46 points).
Last-hour base rate: 15:00-16:00 fell on 35 of 54 sessions; late-day expiry questions are graded against the time-of-day baseline, not 50/50.

gap_half_share.note: half-way share for gap kept, shock giveback, reaction giveback

overnight_rank_min_nights.note: fewest usable prior nights (no roll, holiday or short night) to rank an overnight measure against

giveback_third.note: stall line for an opening drive

tick_burst_pct.note: same-minute percentile of $TICK bar highs/lows that counts as a burst

big_print_pct.note: a large single 0DTE trade: at or above the size this share of the same 10 minutes' single trades stayed at or under, pooled over up to the last 20 sessions (the largest one in a thousand: 40 to 60 lots at the open on the live tape, where the old 100-lot line was about one in five thousand and the top fifth would be 3 lots). A rank band edge

thin_volume_pct.note: same-clock percentile under which new volume is too thin

min_rank_sessions.note: fewest prior sessions for a same-clock median or a link fit; a rank needs same_clock_min_sessions

skew_steep_rank.note: top-fifth rank of the tilt against the recent sessions at this minute

skew_flat_rank.note: bottom-fifth rank of the tilt against the recent sessions at this minute

move_burst_share.note: one 5-minute chunk's share of the 30-minute move for a burst

vix_curve_flat.note: VIX over three-month VIX (and VIX9D over VIX): at or above is inverted

stress_retreat_share.note: VIX retreat share from its session high for exhaustion

stress_hold_share.note: VIX retreat share under which a bounce is not believed

cushion_thin.note: share of today's call-heavy balance left after a move

wall_touch_sigma.note: beyond or back from a wall

accept_minutes.note: minutes beyond a level for acceptance

mega_one_name_share.note: one name's share of the index move

rebal_window_days.note: last trading days of the month for rebalancing

month_turn_days.note: first trading days of the month

vwap_touch_sigma.note: touch tolerance for the day's volume-weighted average price

night_rank_count.note: nights (or sessions, or weekends) a same-clock rank looks back over

same_clock_min_sessions.note: fewest usable prior sessions to rank a session measure against at the same clock (the owner's rank rule)

groups.purpose: Feed the 09:35-10:30 ten-minute five-way call: gap size, which side of the settled open wins, fresh session extremes, how contested and busy the open is, and how choppy or one-way its path has been.

questions.cadence: once at the 09:35 read on the settled open; answer held as a day constant to 10:30 (code weights it by minutes since the open)
questions.ask: How large was this morning's gap from yesterday's close?
questions.instructions: Read `gap.size`. How large was this morning's gap between yesterday's close and the settled open, whichever way it went, against the recent sessions' gaps?

options.name: small
options.description: the gap was in the bottom third of the recent sessions' gaps

options.name: typical
options.description: the gap was in the middle third of the recent sessions' gaps

options.name: large
options.description: the gap was in the top third of the recent sessions' gaps

criteria: |gap| larger than under a third of the prior sessions' |gap| (bottom third)
|gap| larger than a third to two thirds of them (middle third)
|gap| larger than over two thirds of them (top third)

labels_needed.name: gap.size
labels_needed.example: this morning's gap of 0.44 sigma is larger than 17 of the last 20 days' gaps, top third: price opened above yesterday's close, measured at 09:35 because the 09:30 print uses stale prices; 1.4 times this morning's same-day straddle
labels_needed.computed_how: |09:34 close - prior_close|/sigma_anchor ranked against the same gap on up to the last 20 prior sessions (each its settled open against the prior_close on its first diary row, in its own morning anchor; a session whose anchor was estimated is left out), stated as 'larger than N of the last M days' gaps' and its third (bottom/middle/top); omitted under same_clock_min_sessions usable sessions; then the side it opened on; anchor guard: anchor only from a row stamped by 09:40, else 09:35 sigma_live, else spot*(VIX/100)/sqrt(252) (VIX is quoted in percent), flagged 'ruler estimated'
labels_needed.source: SPX 1-min bars (live Schwab $SPX; replay state/reversion/bars/{day}-SPX.json); state/reversion/{day}.jsonl

questions.why: Gap size sets how busy the first half hour is; it says nothing about the next 10 minutes' direction, so it serves size only and is asked once instead of twelve identical times.
questions.evidence: 59 sessions: |gap| vs first-30 range corr +0.24; signed gap vs next 10 min -0.015 (no direction). Old 'large' (>0.80) fired on 2-3 of 59 days; >=0.40 fires on about 22. Fill by 0.15 sigma rule: under 15/16 filled that day, 0.15-0.40 6/19, over 0.40 5/24.
questions.origin: round1:gap_size (reworded: 3 bands, day constant, no direction claim; bands ranked against the prior sessions' gaps)

questions.cadence: every 5 min 09:45-10:30, from the first read with a live tape unit (code weights by minutes-since-open bucket; the 09:50-10:05 bucket carries the effect)
questions.ask: Which side of the settled open does the opening favour now?
questions.instructions: Read `open.path`. Where price is now, in tape units from the settled open, decides first. Check rotating first. Which side of the settled open does the opening favour now?

options.name: up_firm
options.description: now more than one tape unit above the open, and it has given back less than the stall line of its high

options.name: up_fading
options.description: now more than one tape unit above the open, but it has given back the stall line or more of its high

options.name: rotating
options.description: within one tape unit of the open now

options.name: down_fading
options.description: now more than one tape unit below the open, but it has given back the stall line or more of its low

options.name: down_firm
options.description: now more than one tape unit below the open, and it has given back less than the stall line of its low

criteria.down_fading: mirror of up_fading below the open
criteria.down_firm: mirror of up_firm below the open

labels_needed.name: open.path
labels_needed.example: 20 minutes after the settled open, price reached 0.22 sigma above it and 0.04 sigma below it, crossed it once, and gave back 18% of its high, under the stall line; price is now 1.6 tape units above the settled open (one tape unit = the typical 5-minute swing right now, 0.11 sigma), more than one tape unit away on the up side, on the gap's side
labels_needed.computed_how: settled open = 09:34 close; high/low since, giveback share against giveback_third ('under / at or past the stall line'), where price sits now in today's tape unit (rulers.ruler: the median high-low range of the last three finished 5-minute slices, floored at ruler_floor_sigma, in the morning anchor): more than one unit either side is away, within one (inclusive) rotating; gap-side clause (on / against the gap's side, or 'with no real gap this morning' when the gap ranks in the bottom third of the last {night_rank_count} sessions' gaps; left out while the gap has no rank); omitted while the unit is held (before 09:45) or the bars have stopped

questions.why: Replaces opening_drive's seven options with five signed ones: stalling and failed flipped sign between windows on 10-24 reads, and tested_then_reversed fired on 2 of 59 days.
questions.evidence: Lane grading, 59 sessions: driving_up continued 47/24, driving_down 33/32; >0.10 sigma from the open continued 32 vs 15 at 09:50-10:05 but 56 vs 49 at 10:10-10:30; held-out Brier of the old form -0.05%. Round-3 check (fix12/chk.py, 649 reads 09:40-10:30): the reordered rules give exactly one answer on every read (rotating 246, up_firm 138, down_firm 167, down_fading 65, up_fading 33); the old rules left 90 reads unanswered and 226 double-answered.

questions.cadence: every 5 min 09:45-10:30 with a 5-minute window; then every 30-minute read with a 30-minute window
questions.ask: Did price just set a new session high or low, or stall near one?
questions.instructions: Read `open.fresh_extreme` and `price.day_range_position`. Over the window the label names, did price set a new high or low for the session, or is it sitting near one without setting a new one? Check in order: both_new, new_high, new_low, stalled_near_high, stalled_near_low, middle.

options.name: new_high
options.description: price set a new session high in the window and no new low

options.name: new_low
options.description: price set a new session low in the window and no new high

options.name: both_new
options.description: price set both a new high and a new low in the window

options.name: stalled_near_high
options.description: no new extreme in the window, and price sits in the top band of today's range

options.name: stalled_near_low
options.description: no new extreme in the window, and price sits in the bottom band of today's range

options.name: middle
options.description: no new extreme, and price sits between the top and bottom bands of today's range

criteria.new_high: max high of the window's bars > session high before them; no new low

labels_needed.name: open.fresh_extreme
labels_needed.example: in the last 5 minutes price set a new session high, 0.05 sigma above the earlier high from 09:52; it now sits 0.02 sigma below that high, in the top band of today's 0.31 sigma range (past the 75% line); it is above the first-15-minute range, which it first broke at 10:01
labels_needed.computed_how: max/min of the last window's bars vs the session extreme before them; day-range band against range_top_share / range_bottom_share; opening-range break clause (first 15 minutes)

labels_needed.name: price.day_range_position
labels_needed.example: price is in the top band of today's range so far (past the 75% line), 96% of the way up
labels_needed.computed_how: built (engine) with thirds; reworded to the top/bottom band set by range_top_share / range_bottom_share

questions.why: The one opening state with positive held-out skill on the lane's own grading; it folds the opening-range break in as a label clause because the break carries almost nothing once the fresh extreme is known.
questions.evidence: 09:50-10:30, 59 sessions: new_high next 10 min up 53% / down 31% (n=118, 31 days), new_low down 44% / up 27% (n=125, 38 days); both halves agree; leave-one-day-out Brier +1.45% (15-min range alone +0.38%). Day-clustered 25 with / 21 against / 11 tied, so it lives on trend mornings.
questions.origin: new (review: opening-hour direction); absorbs deferred opening_range_status and opening_range_break

questions.ask: How contested has the settled open been so far?
questions.instructions: Read `open.settled_open_crosses`. How contested has the settled open been so far, against the same minute on the recent sessions?

options.name: one_sided
options.description: price's count of crossings of the settled open so far ranks in the bottom third of the recent sessions' counts to this minute (a tie is not beaten)

options.name: some_crossing
options.description: price's count of crossings of the settled open so far ranks in the middle third of the recent sessions' counts to this minute (a tie is not beaten)

options.name: contested
options.description: price's count of crossings of the settled open so far ranks in the top third of the recent sessions' counts to this minute (a tie is not beaten)

criteria.one_sided: crosses beat under {third_lo} of the last {night_rank_count} sessions' crosses to this minute (bottom third; a tie is not beaten)
criteria.some_crossing: crosses beat {third_lo} to {third_hi} of them (middle third)
criteria.contested: crosses beat over {third_hi} of them (top third)

labels_needed.name: open.settled_open_crosses
labels_needed.example: price sits 0.01 sigma above the settled open; since it was set 25 minutes ago price has crossed it 6 times, more often than 17 of the last 20 sessions had by this minute, top third: contested
labels_needed.computed_how: where price sits against the settled open (09:34 close) first; then the count of 1-minute closes since 09:35 switching side of it (a close on it keeps its side), ranked against the same count from each prior session's own settled open to this clock minute on up to the last {night_rank_count} sessions (every session with bars counts: a count is not in sigma, so an estimated ruler does not leave a day out; a tie is not beaten), said as 'more often than N of the last M sessions had by this minute' and its third, bottom one-sided / middle some crossing / top contested ('no more often than any' when it beats none); omitted under {same_clock_min_sessions} sessions with the rank's reason

questions.why: Repeated fights over the settled open mean two-way flow is active: the next 10 minutes run larger, even after a quiet 5 minutes, which moves weight out of the five-way flat bucket. Crossings pile up with the minutes since the open, so the count is judged against the same minute on the recent sessions, not a fixed count. Asked from 09:45, when ten minutes of path exist (open.chop and the tape unit go live then): at 09:40 five bars give 0 to 2 crossings and 2 already ranks top third. Crossings are small whole numbers and a tie is not beaten, so the thirds come out uneven (about 42/25/32% bottom/middle/top over 09:40-10:30 on 39 replayed days).
questions.evidence: 649 opening reads: flat-in-10 by crosses 0.37 / 0.40 / 0.36 / 0.28 (6+, median move 0.083 vs about 0.058 sigma); inside last-5-minute terciles 0-1 vs 2+ crosses 0.48/0.40, 0.40/0.34, 0.31/0.27.

questions.cadence: every 5 min 09:45-10:30 (asleep while the tape unit is held before 09:45)
questions.ask: How busy is the opening for this time of day?
questions.instructions: Read `tape.unit_vs_normal` and `range.today_vs_normal`. Check very_busy first. How busy is the opening right now for this time of day?

options.name: quiet
options.description: the tape unit and today's range both in the bottom third for this time of day, or one in the bottom third and the other in the middle third

options.name: normal
options.description: both in the middle third for this time of day, or one in the top third and the other in the bottom third

options.name: busy
options.description: one in the top third for this time of day and the other in the middle third

options.name: very_busy
options.description: both in the top third for this time of day, or the tape unit wider than all of the recent sessions

criteria: both bottom third, or one bottom one middle
both middle, or one top one bottom
one top third, one middle
both top third, or the wider-than-all flag

labels_needed.name: tape.unit_vs_normal
labels_needed.example: the tape unit (the middle of the last three 5-minute ranges) is 0.10 sigma, wider than 14 of the last 19 sessions at 10:05, in the top third
labels_needed.computed_how: state_builder.ruler + rulers.unit_rank in sigma_anchor: the unit ranked against the same three slices at this minute on up to the last {night_rank_count} prior sessions, each in its own anchor with 'ruler estimated' sessions left out, at least {same_clock_min_sessions} of them; omitted while held before 09:45

labels_needed.name: range.today_vs_normal
labels_needed.example: today's range so far is 0.73% of its opening price, larger than 17 of the last 20 sessions at this time of day, top third
labels_needed.computed_how: the day's high-low so far (spot included) over its first bar's open, ranked against the same share to this clock on up to the last {night_rank_count} prior sessions (ranks.rank_sessions; a share of price, so every session with bars counts), at least {same_clock_min_sessions} of them, else omitted with the reason; said as 'larger than N of the last M sessions at this time of day' and its third

questions.why: The median of three 5-minute ranges is the lane's own outcome unit and forecasts the next 10 minutes better than the last 5 minutes, which also carries the stale 09:30 catch-up.
questions.evidence: Next-10 range 09:45-10:30, n=540: tape unit Spearman 0.509, last-5 range 0.432, sigma_anchor 0.379. Median 09:30-09:34 range 0.169 sigma vs 0.102 for 09:35-09:39.
questions.origin: round1:opening_pace (input swapped to the tape unit rank)

questions.ask: How choppy or one-way has the open been since the settled open?
questions.instructions: Read `open.chop`. Since the settled open, has price's path been choppy, mixed or one-way, against the same minute on the recent sessions?

options.name: choppy
options.description: the path since the settled open is in the bottom third of the recent sessions' paths to this minute for how one-way it was: price travelled far for little net move

options.name: mixed
options.description: the path is in the middle third of the recent sessions' paths to this minute

options.name: one_way
options.description: the path is in the top third of the recent sessions' paths to this minute: most of the distance travelled went one way

criteria.choppy: path efficiency beats under {third_lo} of the last {night_rank_count} sessions' at this minute (bottom third; a tie is not beaten)

labels_needed.name: open.chop
labels_needed.example: since the settled open 25 minutes ago price travelled 0.45 sigma to end 0.03 sigma below it (path efficiency 0.07, the net move over the distance travelled) and crossed it 4 times; that path is more one-way than 6 of the last 20 sessions at this minute, bottom third: choppy
labels_needed.computed_how: path efficiency (measures.path_efficiency) of the 1-minute closes from the settled open (the 09:34 close) to the last finished bar: |net move| over the distance travelled close to close, 0 to 1; ranked against the same path efficiency from each prior session's own settled open to this clock minute on up to the last {night_rank_count} sessions (every session whose closes moved counts: a share, not in sigma, so an estimated ruler does not leave a day out; a tie is not beaten), said as 'more one-way than N of the last M sessions at this minute' and its third, bottom choppy / middle mixed / top one-way ('no more one-way than any' when it beats none); the distance travelled and the net move in sigma and the crossings of the open are said beside it as facts; omitted before 09:45 ('the path since the open is judged from 09:45, when ten minutes of it exist'), when price has not moved from the settled open, and under {same_clock_min_sessions} sessions with the rank's reason

questions.why: Owner decision #10 (2026-09-27): whether the open has been chopping around the settled open or travelling one way is a regime read the five-way call lacks; open_contested counts the fights over one level, this measures the whole path. Path efficiency falls with the minutes since the open, so it is judged against the same minute on the recent sessions, not a fixed line.
questions.evidence: Replay, 59 sessions of bars (2026-07-06 to 09-25), 390 reads 09:45-10:30 every 5 minutes on the 39 days with 20 prior sessions: next-10-minute price move with the open's net side 57% on top-third (one-way) reads (82/145; 64% and 53% by halves), 49% on the bottom third (66/134), 45% in the middle (49/109); median next-10-minute |move| barely differs by third (5.9 / 6.4 / 5.7 basis points), so it carries direction context, not size. Weak and unproven: live until the learning loop weighs it.

options.name: both_selling

Not re-measured on the ranked definition (a large trade is one in the largest one in a thousand of the same 10 minutes' single trades on up to the last 20 sessions, about 40 to 60 lots; the lean in thirds against those sessions); the next replay must measure it, on ts-sorted tape.

labels_needed.computed_how: the price.recent_move rank first (bottom third: no real move to shape); then the largest of the six 5-minute chunks over the net 30-minute move (burst line move_burst_share, a share of the move's own net) and path efficiency = net over the sum of 1-minute moves, today's and each prior session's alike from the close before the half hour through its finished bar closes, ranked against the same measure to this clock on up to the last night_rank_count prior sessions (ranks.rank_sessions), stated as 'more one-way than N of the last M sessions at this minute' and its third (bottom/middle/top); ties are not beaten; omitted under same_clock_min_sessions usable sessions, with the reason; every prior session with bars counts, its ruler estimated or not, since no ruler scales this measure; bottom third = choppy

Gap correlation with next 60 rises through the day (+0.19 morning to +0.26 at 13:30-15:00), so it runs to 14:32.

criteria.extending: one side, beyond now, reach rank above {third_hi} against the furthest any bar had gone past either first-hour edge by this clock on those of the last {night_rank_count} sessions that had broken one by then, at least {same_clock_min_sessions} of them

questions.why: A trend-versus-noise read anchored at the higher and lower of the open and yesterday's close; kept as a regime read, not as the source strategy's Sharpe. The move from the open grows with the minutes since it, so how far price has stretched past the band's anchors is judged against the same minute on the recent sessions, not against their average move and a fixed edge distance.
questions.evidence: Measured on the earlier band (the 14-session average move, a 0.05 sigma edge), not yet on the ranked one: station replay at half-hour marks: above the band next 30 min up 53/83 (64%), below it down 28/59 (47%); another replay 51-53% beyond vs 43-45% inside, no edge after 13:00. The Zarattini Sharpe comes from stops and sizing, not a hit rate.

options.name: middle

options.name: wide

criteria: band/reach over the next 30 minutes ranks below {third_lo} against the same share at this minute on the last {night_rank_count} sessions (bottom third)
rank {third_lo} to {third_hi} (middle third)
rank above {third_hi} (top third)

labels_needed.name: ruler.flat_band_reach
labels_needed.example: the next-30-minute flat band is 0.07 sigma; a typical 30-minute move now (tape and straddle combined) is 0.08 sigma, so the band covers 0.84 of it, more than on 14 of the last 16 sessions at this time of day, top third; the next-60-minute flat band is 0.11 sigma; a typical 60-minute move is 0.12 sigma, so the band covers 0.93 of it

groups.purpose: The dark news feed seen through the tape: sudden bursts, whether they set extremes, the reaction path after any release or burst, vol's reaction, what moved with the shock, and single-name shocks.

questions.instructions: Read `shock.burst`. Price had a sudden burst in the last hour: a five-minute move larger than the biggest five-minute move of the hour to that minute (from the settled open when that is shorter) on every one of the recent sessions. What has happened since? Check in order: fresh, round_trip, settling.

options.name: round_trip

questions.why: News with no feed shows up as a burst far bigger than the tape usually moves at that time of day; volatility clusters, so a fresh or round-tripped shock means a busier next half hour, even when the net move looks small. Every window is ranked against the biggest five-minute move of the same hour on recent sessions, so an hour of windows does not throw up a shock by chance.
questions.evidence: 64 episodes on 37/59 days; shock minutes P(|next 30|>0.10) 0.41 vs 0.32, median range 0.183 vs 0.143; 14:00 hour 0.43 vs 0.21; next-30 size 1.29/1.41/1.56x the clock median at 4x/5x/6x bursts. Adds size beyond the last 30 minutes only when the net move is small (0.30 vs 0.24). Opening bursts (top 5% for the minute): with the morning 16/7, against 12/12 (folded as a label clause).

questions.why: The usual idea is that bitcoin is a fast risk gauge the index follows. Measured here, it runs the other way. When bitcoin has run ahead of the index in the last half hour, the index's next half hour leans slightly the opposite way. At the minute level the index leads bitcoin, not the reverse. The label reports the move and the link and does not say 'bitcoin leads', so the learning loop learns the sign.
questions.evidence: 1,474 half-hours on 134 sessions (2026-03-17 to 09-25, 5-min bars): excess vs SPX next 30 min rank corr -0.074 (p<0.01; day-clustered t -1.97 controlling for SPX's own last 30). Top fifth: SPX next 30 up 43.5%, mean -2.1 bp (about a quarter of the median 7.9 bp half-hour move); other fifths 51-56% up. Same sign in both halves of the sample (-0.069, -0.078); stronger when the link is tight (-0.10, p 0.01) than loose (-0.04, ns). On 08-11 to 09-25 alone (n 363) -0.03, ns, which matches the earlier xasset study (+0.02, n 1,089 one-minute windows). Minute lead-lag, 33 sessions: corr(bitcoin[t-1], SPX[t]) 0.009, corr(SPX[t-1], bitcoin[t]) 0.047, same minute 0.31. The index leads.

questions.why: Bitcoin's tie to stocks comes and goes. Since 2020 the 60-session correlation of daily moves has run from -0.09 to 0.72. This year the 20-session figure fell from about 0.7 in March and April to 0.26 in August. A tight day says one risk mood is driving both markets. A loose day says bitcoin is on its own news, and its moves say little about stocks. This question tells the loop which days to trust the other bitcoin reads on.
questions.evidence: Indirect only. The btc_gap_30m effect is -0.10 (p 0.01) on tight-link half-hours and -0.04 (ns) on loose ones, 737 each. Whether the link level on its own leans the index's direction is untested. Daily CME bitcoin vs SPX correlation: 20-session 0.63 and 60-session 0.39 as of 2026-09-25; 260-session 0.51.

labels_needed.name: xasset.btc_five_day
labels_needed.example: over the last 5 sessions bitcoin futures (/MBT) did 3.2 normal weeks better than the index's move would match, in the top fifth of the last 15 5-session stretches, higher than 14 of them; the index itself rose 0.8 of its normal week
labels_needed.computed_how: bitcoin's simple return over the last five sessions, close to close (the index's last bar at each session's close, 16:00 or 13:00 on a half day, and bitcoin's newest bar within {window_10_min} minutes before it), minus its usual multiple of the index's x SPX's five-session return; the multiple is fitted (bitcoin.slope) on bitcoin's daily returns against SPX's over the last {night_rank_count} + 5 sessions with both on one contract; ranked in fifths against the five sessions ending on each of up to the last {night_rank_count} sessions before, needing {same_clock_min_sessions} of them; 'normal week' = median |five-session excess| over those; it sleeps while a roll is pending, and leaves the Thursday roll evening out of its daily moves
labels_needed.source: the overnight store's /MBT bars at each prior session's 16:00 (its nights reach back to March) and SPX's saved closes (state/reversion/bars); the roll guard applies (a five-session window across a /MBT roll is left out)

questions.why: The 'canary' idea is that bitcoin weakening while stocks hold up warns of a stock drop. The data does not support it. From 2020 to 2026, weeks when bitcoin lagged were followed by slightly better index days, not worse. The pattern was not stable in 2025-26. It is in the set because it is the most common bitcoin-for-stocks claim, and the loop should learn its sign rather than JEV assuming it.
questions.evidence: 1,608 sessions 2020-2026 (daily /BTC vs $SPX): bitcoin lagging (bottom fifth) -> SPX next day up 57.9% (+12.5 bp), middle 54.0% (+6.1 bp), bitcoin ahead (top fifth) 51.5% (-0.3 bp). Rank corr with the next day -0.004 (p 0.89); with the next five sessions (non-overlapping) -0.056 (p 0.32). Since mid-2022 the same shape (59.8 / 52.3 / 51.7% up). 2025-26 (n 429): bottom 62.6%, middle 49.0%, top 66.3%. The shape breaks.

questions.ask: Did bitcoin move further overnight than S&P futures did, and which way?
questions.instructions: Read `overnight.btc_vs_futures`. Since the S&P futures' 16:00 price, or on the first session after a weekend or holiday since the futures reopened the evening before (bitcoin's weekend itself is a question of its own), did bitcoin move further than the futures' own move over the same span would match, in the direction that has gone with stocks rising, or in the direction that has gone with stocks falling?

options.name: btc_ahead_up
options.description: bitcoin went further than the futures' move would match, in the direction that has gone with stocks rising over the recent nights

options.name: btc_ahead_down
options.description: bitcoin went further than the futures' move would match, in the direction that has gone with stocks falling over the recent nights

criteria.btc_ahead_up: the gap to the futures ranks in the outer fifth on the side that has gone with stocks rising, against the last {night_rank_count} nights: >= {top_fifth} while bitcoin's usual multiple of the futures is at or above zero, <= {bottom_fifth} while it is below
criteria.btc_ahead_down: the outer fifth on the side that has gone with stocks falling: <= {bottom_fifth} while the multiple is at or above zero, >= {top_fifth} while it is below

questions.sleep_when: excess rank in the middle three fifths; the Thursday bitcoin roll night or a roll pending; fewer than {overnight_rank_min_nights} clean prior nights; no /MBT trade in the last {window_10_min} minutes before the read

labels_needed.name: overnight.btc_vs_futures
labels_needed.example: S&P futures stand 0.31 sigma below their 16:00 price; since then bitcoin futures (/MBT) fell 1.9 of its normal nights to this time, 1.4 normal gaps below what the futures' move would match, bottom fifth of the last 20 nights; over those nights bitcoin up has gone with stocks up, so bitcoin is ahead in the stocks-down direction
labels_needed.computed_how: bitcoin's percent move from the night's start to the read (the last bar finished by each time, neither over {window_10_min} minutes old) minus its usual multiple of the /ES percent move over the same span (fitted by bitcoin.slope over the same span to the same minute on the last {night_rank_count} nights); the night starts at the prior session's close (16:00, 13:00 after a half day), or on the first session after a weekend or holiday at the end of the S&P futures' first minute after their 18:00 reopen, so the weekend (weekend.btc_path) is left out and the sentence says 'since the S&P futures reopened at 18:00 Sunday'; ranked in fifths against the same span on the prior nights with both on one contract (at least {overnight_rank_min_nights}); 'normal night' = median |move| of those nights, for bitcoin and for its gap to the futures; the figure says in_line when the gap sits in the middle three fifths (the gate sleeps the question). Roll guard: Schwab's /BTC and /MBT history is one stitched front-month series; it switches contract at 18:00 ET on the Thursday before the last-Friday expiry and jumps up 0.28-0.53% against IBIT (7 of 7 rolls, Mar-Sep 2026), about a third of a normal night. The roll night is left out, and so is a read with a roll pending (rolls.pending).
labels_needed.source: the overnight store (state/spx_jev/overnight/{day}.jsonl): Schwab /MBT (micro bitcoin futures) 1- and 5-minute bars with extended hours, contract stamped (the front contract: /MBTV26 now, /MBTX26 from 18:00 ET Thu 10-29); /BTC is saved beside it as a cross-check (the same price, under 5 bars an hour on Saturdays). /ES as in overnight_move_vs_expected.

questions.why: Bitcoin trades through the night and reacts to the same risk news as stocks. If it has moved further than futures, the thought is that stocks have not caught up yet. The data says futures already have: bitcoin's overnight move sits inside the gap (rank correlation +0.63 with the SPX open gap) and adds nothing after 09:30. It is here so the learning loop can confirm that, and because the owner asked for bitcoin in the pre-open read.
questions.evidence: 119 clean nights (2026-03 to 09, 5-min bars; roll and /ES-roll nights removed): bitcoin excess over futures vs SPX 09:35-10:05 rank corr +0.01 (p 0.91), vs 09:35-10:35 +0.05, vs 09:35-close -0.05. Fifths: bottom fifth first 30 min up 64%, top fifth 57%, middle 43% (no order). Halves: -0.10 then +0.11 (sign flips). The round-3 figure (+0.15/+0.24, n=31) does not hold at four times the sample. Long sample, 287 weekends 2020-26: bitcoin's weekend move is in the Monday gap (+0.19; +0.36 since mid-2022) but predicts nothing after it (Monday open-to-close -0.06, t -1.5 controlling for the gap).

questions.ask: After a big bitcoin weekend, did bitcoin keep going, hold, or turn back once S&P futures reopened?
questions.instructions: Read `weekend.btc_path`. It gives bitcoin's weekend leg (from Friday's close until S&P futures reopened on Sunday evening) and its reopen leg (since the reopen). Taking the weekend leg's direction as the reference, did the reopen leg extend it, hold it, or turn back against it?

options.name: extended
options.description: after S&P futures reopened, bitcoin kept moving the same way as its weekend move

options.name: held
options.description: after the reopen bitcoin stayed about where the weekend left it

options.name: reversed
options.description: after the reopen bitcoin moved back against its weekend move

criteria.extended: reopen-leg rank vs the last {night_rank_count} reopen legs in the weekend leg's direction >= {third_hi}
criteria.held: reopen-leg rank in the middle third
criteria.reversed: reopen-leg rank against the weekend leg's direction >= {third_hi}

questions.sleep_when: weekend leg not in the top third by size of the last {night_rank_count} weekends (an ordinary weekend); not the first session after a weekend or holiday; fewer than {overnight_rank_min_nights} prior weekends; a bitcoin roll across either leg; no trade in the last {window_60_min} minutes of the weekend leg (the Saturday maintenance window)

labels_needed.name: weekend.btc_path
labels_needed.example: S&P futures stand 0.64 sigma above their 16:00 price; bitcoin futures (/MBT) fell 0.4 of its normal weekends from the Friday 16:00 close to the S&P futures' reopen at 18:00 Sunday, larger than 4 of the last 15 weekends by size, bottom third; since the reopen it has moved 4.0 of a normal reopen leg back against it, bottom third of those weekends' reopen legs taken their weekend's way: it turned back
labels_needed.computed_how: two bitcoin legs, each a percent move between the last bars finished by the two times: the weekend leg from the prior session's close (16:00, or 13:00 after a half day) to the S&P futures' reopen after their longest halt since that close, found in their bars (Sunday 18:00 after a weekend), and the reopen leg from there to the read. A price at the close or the read over {window_10_min} minutes old, or at the reopen over {window_60_min}, leaves it out. The weekend leg is ranked by size against the last {night_rank_count} weekends, the top third a big weekend, (the first sessions after a weekend or holiday); the reopen leg, taken the weekend leg's way, in thirds against those weekends' reopen legs taken theirs: extended in the top third, reversed in the bottom, held between. Each is said in shares of its own median |leg| over those weekends; the sentence opens with where the S&P futures stand against their 16:00 price. Roll guard: Schwab's /BTC and /MBT history is one stitched front-month series; it switches contract at 18:00 ET on the Thursday before the last-Friday expiry and jumps up 0.28-0.53% against IBIT (7 of 7 rolls, Mar-Sep 2026), about a third of a normal night. The roll night is left out, and so is a read with a roll pending (rolls.pending).
labels_needed.source: the overnight store (state/spx_jev/overnight/{day}.jsonl): Schwab /MBT (micro bitcoin futures) 1- and 5-minute bars with extended hours, contract stamped (the front contract: /MBTV26 now, /MBTX26 from 18:00 ET Thu 10-29); /BTC is saved beside it as a cross-check (the same price, under 5 bars an hour on Saturdays). Before 2026-05-29 CME bitcoin futures were shut Fri 17:00 to Sun 18:00 ET, so older weekends have only the Sunday reopen gap and no path; only weekends from 2026-05-29 are ranked.

questions.why: Bitcoin is the one big market that trades all weekend, so it shows first how risk appetite moved while stocks were shut. A peer-reviewed study (Mourey, Shahrour, Soiman, Finance Research Letters 2025) finds that weak crypto weekends predict weaker Mondays for stocks and strong ones do not, an effect that grew after the May 2022 LUNA collapse. That study measures Friday close to Monday close, and at 09:28 the futures gap already contains most of it. This question asks the part the gap does not show: whether bitcoin's weekend verdict is being confirmed or taken back since futures reopened.
questions.evidence: No direct test: only 17 weekends of 24/7 CME bitcoin exist (since 2026-05-29). Long sample, 277 ranked weekends 2020-26 (Fri close to Sun reopen): bottom-fifth bitcoin weekends had the SPX Monday gap at -23 bp on average, then Monday open-to-close +20 bp, up 60%, the same as ordinary weekends (61%). Since mid-2022, n=44: gap -32 bp, open-to-close +9 bp, up 55%. The weakness shows up in the gap and is not extended after it. Cases: 2022-05-09 and 2022-06-13 (bitcoin -4.6%, -6.4%), SPX extended lower after the open (-2.2%, -2.3%); 2024-08-05 (bitcoin -6.7%), SPX gapped down 3.7% and closed +0.7% above the open.

labels.example: the reaction starts at 10:00 with the University of Michigan's consumer sentiment report (expected at that time); in its first 15 minutes price fell 0.40 normal-day sigma, larger than 19 of the last 19 sessions over the same 15 minutes, each in its own sigma, top third; since then it has given back 87% of it, past the half line, and has not crossed back through where the reaction started; this was scheduled economic data
labels.computed_how: anchor = release, follow-on (press conference, testimony Q&A) when due within 45 minutes, or detected burst (shock.burst); every figure of today's in normal-day sigma (20-session median sigma_anchor), since an event swells today's own anchor; the first reaction's |move| over its first 15 minutes ranked with ranks.rank_sessions against the same 15 minutes, event or not, each session's in its own sigma (the sentence says so), on up to the last 20 prior sessions (newest first; a session whose morning ruler was estimated is left out), needing same_clock_min_sessions of them, else the label is omitted with the rank's reason; stated as 'N of the last M sessions' and its third; the bottom third sleeps the question; kind named (economic data / Fed remarks / unscheduled); extension against reaction_extend_sigma; giveback against the half line
labels.source: SPX 1-min bars (live Schwab $SPX; replay state/reversion/bars/{day}-SPX.json); calendar

labels.name: flows.etf_creations
labels.example: SPY created 12M shares since the open

labels.name: flows.rebalance_side
labels.example: this quarter stocks beat long Treasuries by 3.9 percentage points of price return (S&P 500 +3.1%, TLT about -0.8%), more than at 19 of the last 24 quarter-ends, top fifth; this month the gap is 0.8 percentage points, an ordinary month; today closes the quarter, so the quarter gap governs today: top fifth
labels.computed_how: SPX price return (no total-return index was probed) minus TLT (20+ year Treasuries) return (fallback: -8 x change in $TNX yield, before 15:00 only) since the prior month-end and quarter-end close; each ranked against its own last 24 months/quarters; names which gap governs today (the quarter gap in a quarter's last days, else the month gap)

labels.name: gap.fill_progress
labels.example: the gap up is losing ground after 116 minutes: price sits 0.26 sigma above yesterday's close and keeps 88% of the 0.30 sigma gap, at or above the half line; it first touched yesterday's close (within 0.02 sigma) 85 minutes ago; the gap was larger than 10 of the last 19 days' gaps, middle third, a real gap
labels.computed_how: current location first, then history: share of the gap kept, stated as 'keeps N%, above/below the half line' (gap_half_share; never 'given back', which asks JEV to subtract); touch of prior_close within gap_touch_sigma; then the gap's rank ('larger than N of the last M days' gaps' and its third); a real gap is one larger than the bottom third of the last {night_rank_count} sessions' gaps (gap_open.gap_rank: |settled open - prior close| in each day's own morning anchor, estimated-anchor days left out, a tie not beaten); under {same_clock_min_sessions} usable sessions the label is omitted with the rank's reason; on a day with no real gap it says so with the rank ('there was no real gap: ... a gap larger than N of the last M days' gaps, bottom third')

labels.name: gap.morning_vs_gap
labels.example: from the settled open to 11:30 price fell 0.11 sigma, against this morning's 0.30 sigma gap up (larger than 10 of the last 19 days' gaps, middle third), and touched yesterday's close; it now sits 0.26 sigma above it
labels.computed_how: 09:34 close to the 11:29 close vs gap sign; touch flag; the gap's rank in brackets; omitted on a day with no real gap (a real gap is one larger than the bottom third of the last {night_rank_count} sessions' gaps (gap_open.gap_rank: |settled open - prior close| in each day's own morning anchor, estimated-anchor days left out, a tie not beaten); under {same_clock_min_sessions} usable sessions the label is omitted with the rank's reason)

labels.name: gap.reach_distance
labels.example: yesterday's close is 0.30 sigma below price, 1.9 typical 60-minute moves away
labels.computed_how: distance to prior_close in sigma and in 60-minute reach units

labels.name: gap.size
labels.example: this morning's gap of 0.44 sigma is larger than 17 of the last 20 days' gaps, top third: price opened above yesterday's close, measured at 09:35 because the 09:30 print uses stale prices; 1.4 times this morning's same-day straddle
labels.computed_how: |09:34 close - prior_close|/sigma_anchor ranked against the same gap on up to the last 20 prior sessions (each its settled open against the prior_close on its first diary row, in its own morning anchor; a session whose anchor was estimated is left out), stated as 'larger than N of the last M days' gaps' and its third (bottom/middle/top); omitted under same_clock_min_sessions usable sessions; then the side it opened on; anchor guard: anchor only from a row stamped by 09:40, else 09:35 sigma_live, else spot*(VIX/100)/sqrt(252) (VIX is quoted in percent), flagged 'ruler estimated'
labels.source: SPX 1-min bars (live Schwab $SPX; replay state/reversion/bars/{day}-SPX.json); state/reversion/{day}.jsonl

labels.name: gex.balance_vs_yesterday
labels.example: the same book leaned to calls at yesterday's close too, under the usual assumption that dealers hold the calls and are short the puts, so it has not tipped overnight
labels.computed_how: last RTH gex_views.regime of the prior diary day vs now; never net_exposure (disagrees with gex_views on 15% of rows)

labels.name: gex.book_balance
labels.example: at the current price, same-day call positions carry more gamma than put positions, both by open interest and by today's volume, under the usual assumption that dealers hold the calls and are short the puts; the balance would tip to puts 0.61 sigma lower
labels.computed_how: gex_views.regime (open interest) and regime_0dte_vol mapped long->'call positions carry more gamma', short->'put positions carry more gamma', uncertain->'too close to call'; tip distance = |spot - flip|/sigma; omitted when the 0DTE book is dead

labels.name: gex.charm_wall_distance
labels.example: the charm wall of today's same-day book (the strike where its delta decay piles up) sits 0.22 sigma above price, farther from price than on 13 of the last 19 sessions at this minute, top third: far from price, 2.8 remaining straddles away
labels.computed_how: |gex_views.charm_wall - spot|/sigma_anchor ranked with ranks.rank_sessions against each session's charm-wall distance on its diary row at this minute, in its own ruler, on up to the last 20 prior sessions (newest first; a session whose morning ruler was estimated is left out), needing same_clock_min_sessions of them, else the label is omitted with the rank's reason; stated as 'N of the last M sessions' and its third; remaining straddles beside it

labels.name: gex.cushion_if_moved
labels.example: a drop of 0.5 sigma would tip same-day gamma from call-heavy to put-heavy, under the usual assumption that dealers hold the calls and are short the puts; a rise of the same size leaves it call-heavy, above the thin line
labels.computed_how: slide_flip(zero, spot +/- 0.5 sigma) in lefteye_gex_box.py:530 needs the full options chain (contracts); the diary row only carries per-strike gamma at the current price
labels.source: scan change: reversion_lens writes gex_views.cushion_{up,down} from slide_flip(zero, spot +/- 0.5 sigma)

labels.name: gex.delta_weight_side
labels.example: 43% of the directional exposure across the 0-to-7-day books, under the usual assumption that dealers hold the calls and are short the puts, sits at strikes above price, a larger share than on 14 of the last 19 sessions at this minute, top third: more of it above price than usual
labels.computed_how: built (engine) dex_views.dex_above_spot, ranked with ranks.rank_sessions against the same share on each session's diary row at this minute, on up to the last 20 prior sessions (newest first; a session whose morning ruler was estimated is left out), needing same_clock_min_sessions of them, else the label is omitted with the rank's reason; stated as 'N of the last M sessions' and its third: top third more of it above price than usual, bottom third more below, middle about as usual; never a side of price, since a top-third share can be under half

labels.name: gex.flip_distance
labels.example: price is 0.60 sigma above the gamma flip, the level where today's same-day book switches between call-heavy and put-heavy gamma under the usual assumption that dealers hold the calls and are short the puts; farther from price than on 13 of the last 18 sessions at this minute, top third: far from the flip; it has not crossed the flip in the last 30 minutes
labels.computed_how: (spot - gex_views.flip)/sigma_anchor; |distance| ranked with ranks.rank_sessions against each session's |spot - flip| on its diary row at this minute, in its own ruler, on up to the last 20 prior sessions (newest first; a session whose morning ruler was estimated is left out), needing same_clock_min_sessions of them, else the label is omitted with the rank's reason; stated as 'N of the last M sessions' and its third; the top third is far; cross flag vs the row 30 minutes earlier; never says what the flip does to price

labels.name: gex.magnet_distance
labels.example: today's heaviest same-day strike (the magnet) sits 0.09 sigma above price, farther from price than on 10 of the last 19 sessions at this minute, middle third: near it; its grip (top-strike share) is stronger than on 6 of the last 19 sessions at 15:31 ET, below the median; it is the same strike as 30 minutes ago; over the last 30 minutes price sat 0.05 sigma from it on average, farther than on 5 of the last 19 sessions at this minute, bottom third: held there
labels.computed_how: gex_views.magnet; |magnet - spot|/sigma_anchor, the last 30 minutes' mean |close - magnet| and pin_top_share, each ranked with ranks.rank_sessions against the same measure at this minute (each distance in its session's own ruler), on up to the last 20 prior sessions (newest first; a session whose morning ruler was estimated is left out), needing same_clock_min_sessions of them, else the label is omitted with the rank's reason; stated as 'N of the last M sessions' and its third; grip against the median (half_rank)

labels.name: gex.settle_pull
labels.example: today's heaviest same-day strike sits 0.09 sigma above price, outside the 0.05 sigma seat distance; that is 1.1 remaining straddles (what today's options still price before the 16:00 settle), more than on 7 of the last 18 sessions at this minute, middle third: in reach; the gamma-weighted centre of the book sits 0.10 sigma below price, outside the seat distance, the other side; the options settle in 28 minutes
labels.computed_how: (gex_views.magnet - spot) in sigma and in remaining straddles (range_ruler.em_points); the straddle count ranked with ranks.rank_sessions against each session's count on its diary row at this minute, on up to the last 20 prior sessions (newest first; a session whose morning ruler was estimated is left out), needing same_clock_min_sessions of them, else the label is omitted with the rank's reason; stated as 'N of the last M sessions' and its third; the top third out of reach; pin_centroid side; settle clock

labels.name: gex.wall_box
labels.example: the heaviest call-side and put-side strikes of today's same-day book are 0.67 sigma apart, wider than on 16 of the last 18 sessions at this minute, top third: a wide box; both have stood at the same strikes for the last 30 minutes
labels.computed_how: (call_wall_gamma - put_wall_gamma)/sigma_anchor ranked with ranks.rank_sessions against each session's width on its diary row at this minute, in its own ruler, on up to the last 20 prior sessions (newest first; a session whose morning ruler was estimated is left out), needing same_clock_min_sessions of them, else the label is omitted with the rank's reason; stated as 'N of the last M sessions' and its third; change vs 30 minutes ago

labels.name: gex.walls_since_30min
labels.example: over the last 30 minutes the call-side heavy strike moved up one strike (0.07 sigma) and the put-side strike stayed put, so the two are further apart
labels.computed_how: strike change vs the row nearest 30 minutes earlier

labels.name: gex.weight_both_books
labels.example: today's same-day options gamma has 48% of it above price, a larger share than on 13 of the last 18 sessions at this minute, top third: more of it above price than usual; the 1-to-7-day book (today's expiry excluded) has 67% of it above price, a larger share than on 17 of the last 18 sessions at this minute, top third: also more of it above price than usual
labels.computed_how: gamma_above_spot share for the 0DTE book; |net_by_strike_tenor| above vs below spot for the 1-to-7-day book (split_tenor keeps 1-7 DTE, so 0DTE is excluded); each share ranked with ranks.rank_sessions against the same book's share on each session's diary row at this minute, on up to the last 20 prior sessions (newest first; a session whose morning ruler was estimated is left out), needing same_clock_min_sessions of them, else the label is omitted with the rank's reason; stated as 'N of the last M sessions' and its third; the top third says more of the book's gamma sits above price than usual, the bottom third more below, the middle third about as usual; the thirds never name which side of price holds most, since a top-third share can be under half

labels.name: leaders.equal_weight_vs_cap_30m
labels.example: equal-weight RSP usually moves 0.75 times the index (SPY), so +0.10 sigma was expected over the last 30 minutes; it rose 0.22 sigma, 0.12 sigma above that, by size higher than 16 of the last 19 sessions at this minute, top third: a split
labels.computed_how: RSP return minus 20-session beta x SPY return, in SPX sigma; its size ranked against the same measure at this clock on up to the last {night_rank_count} sessions, needing {same_clock_min_sessions} (else the label is omitted with the reason) (each session in its own ruler; an estimated ruler sits out); top third = a split
labels.source: Schwab 1-min bars via market_context.py, saved by the context job to state/spx_jev/context/{day}.jsonl (live) and state/spx_jev/context/bars/{day}.jsonl (backfill: python -m spx_jev.market_context --backfill 2026-08-10); the symbol must be in market_context.SYMBOLS (RSP, SPY)

labels.name: leaders.heavyweight_gap
labels.example: from yesterday's close to the settled open MSFT (6.5% of the index) rose 2.3%, adding 0.15 sigma to the open by itself, larger than 14 of the last 18 sessions' largest single-name gaps, top third: a heavyweight shock; the rest of the index gapped up 0.15 sigma, larger than 4 of the last 18 sessions' rest-of-index gaps, bottom third: the rest barely moved
labels.computed_how: weight x overnight return (yesterday's last bar's close to the settled open, 09:34 bar) per top-8 name, in SPX sigma (the morning anchor as a share of the settled open); rest = SPX gap minus the largest contribution; each unsigned and ranked against the same measure at this clock on up to the last {night_rank_count} sessions, needing {same_clock_min_sessions} (else the label is omitted with the reason), every prior session measured the same way with today's names and weights from its own trading day before, in its own anchor (an estimated anchor sits out); thirds; the gate wakes on a top-third contribution; earnings tag not built; no since-open clause
labels.source: Schwab 1-min bars via market_context.py, saved by the context job to state/spx_jev/context/{day}.jsonl (live) and state/spx_jev/context/bars/{day}.jsonl (backfill: python -m spx_jev.market_context --backfill 2026-08-10); the symbol must be in market_context.SYMBOLS (NVDA AAPL MSFT GOOGL GOOG AMZN META AVGO TSLA; TSLA and GOOG are not yet in SYMBOLS) + state/spx_leaders/weights.json (to write, SSGA SPY holdings) + megacap earnings rows (not yet in calendar/events.json)

labels.name: leaders.megacap_cohesion_30m
labels.example: over the last 30 minutes 2 of the 8 largest stocks rose and 6 fell, each by a move above the bottom third of its own at this minute; the larger count, 6, is higher than 19 of the last 20 sessions at this minute, top third: moving together down; MSFT alone supplied 18% of the index's 0.32 sigma fall, under the 33% one-name share; the index's move was higher than 17 of the last 19 sessions at this minute, top third: a real move
labels.computed_how: top-8 by weights.json (GOOG+GOOGL combined); a name counts as moved when its |30-minute return| is above the bottom third of its own on up to the last {night_rank_count} sessions at this minute; the larger of the up and down counts ranked against the same measure at this clock on up to the last {night_rank_count} sessions, needing {same_clock_min_sessions} (else the label is omitted with the reason) (ties not beaten); the index's move ranked as price.recent_move ranks it (ranks.move_rank)
labels.source: Schwab 1-min bars via market_context.py, saved by the context job to state/spx_jev/context/{day}.jsonl (live) and state/spx_jev/context/bars/{day}.jsonl (backfill: python -m spx_jev.market_context --backfill 2026-08-10); the symbol must be in market_context.SYMBOLS

labels.name: leaders.pull_vs_rest_30m
labels.example: over the last 30 minutes the 8 largest names (36% of the index) contributed +0.02 sigma, by size higher than 5 of the last 19 sessions at this minute, bottom third, and the other 64% contributed +0.11 sigma, by size higher than 18 of the last 19 sessions at this minute, top third; only the rest moved (above the bottom third)
labels.computed_how: weight x return summed over the top 8; rest = SPX move minus that; each in SPX sigma, its size ranked against the same measure at this clock on up to the last {night_rank_count} sessions, needing {same_clock_min_sessions} (else the label is omitted with the reason) with today's names and weights; a part moved when above the bottom third
labels.source: Schwab 1-min bars via market_context.py, saved by the context job to state/spx_jev/context/{day}.jsonl (live) and state/spx_jev/context/bars/{day}.jsonl (backfill: python -m spx_jev.market_context --backfill 2026-08-10); the symbol must be in market_context.SYMBOLS

labels.name: leaders.rotation_30m
labels.example: over the last 30 minutes, after allowing for each sector's usual link to the index, financials, discretionary and industrials beat utilities, staples and health care by 0.05 sigma, higher than 14 of the last 19 sessions at this minute, top third: the sensitive sectors ahead
labels.computed_how: mean 30-minute beta residual of XLF, XLY, XLI minus that of XLU, XLP, XLV, in SPX sigma, signed and ranked against the same measure at this clock on up to the last {night_rank_count} sessions, needing {same_clock_min_sessions} (else the label is omitted with the reason); a gap whose sign and third disagree says it is above or below the usual for this minute
labels.source: Schwab 1-min bars via market_context.py, saved by the context job to state/spx_jev/context/{day}.jsonl (live) and state/spx_jev/context/bars/{day}.jsonl (backfill: python -m spx_jev.market_context --backfill 2026-08-10); the symbol must be in market_context.SYMBOLS

labels.name: leaders.semis_vs_index_30m
labels.example: chips (SMH) usually move 1.7 times the index; over the last 30 minutes they beat that by 0.14 sigma, ahead upward: in the top fifth for this half hour, higher than 17 of the last 19 sessions at this minute
labels.computed_how: SMH 30-minute return minus beta x SPX, in SPX sigma, signed and ranked against the same measure at this clock on up to the last {night_rank_count} sessions, needing {same_clock_min_sessions} (else the label is omitted with the reason), in fifths
labels.source: Schwab 1-min bars via market_context.py, saved by the context job to state/spx_jev/context/{day}.jsonl (live) and state/spx_jev/context/bars/{day}.jsonl (backfill: python -m spx_jev.market_context --backfill 2026-08-10); the symbol must be in market_context.SYMBOLS (SMH)

labels.name: leaders.single_name_10m
labels.example: in the last 10 minutes MSFT rose 0.3%, 5.0 times its usual 10-minute move for this time of day, by size higher than 20 of the last 20 sessions at this minute, every one: a name shock, worth +0.02 sigma of SPX at its 6.5% weight; 4 of the other 7 largest also rose by a top-third 10-minute move of their own, at least the 2-name spreading count
labels.computed_how: each top-8 name's |10-minute return| (the minutes since 09:31 before 09:41) ranked against its own at this clock on up to the last {night_rank_count} sessions, needing {same_clock_min_sessions} (else the label is omitted with the reason), every session with the market context kept (a return is in the name's own units); the name highest in its rank (then furthest past its median) is named; a name shock = higher than every one; the others counted when in the top third of their own and the same way; 'times its usual' = over the median of its own; weights.json
labels.source: Schwab 1-min bars via market_context.py, saved by the context job to state/spx_jev/context/{day}.jsonl (live) and state/spx_jev/context/bars/{day}.jsonl (backfill: python -m spx_jev.market_context --backfill 2026-08-10); the symbol must be in market_context.SYMBOLS

labels.name: leaders.size_spread_day
labels.example: since 09:35, after allowing for their usual swing against SPY, QQQ is 0.16 sigma ahead, higher than 13 of the last 19 sessions at this minute, top third: ahead for this time of day; and IWM is 0.73 sigma behind, higher than 2 of the last 19 sessions at this minute, bottom third: behind for this time of day; QQQ leads by 0.89 sigma, by size higher than 17 of the last 19 sessions at this minute, top third: a lead
labels.computed_how: QQQ and IWM since the settled open (09:34 bar) beyond their 20-session beta x SPY, in SPX sigma; each residual signed and ranked against the same measure at this clock on up to the last {night_rank_count} sessions, needing {same_clock_min_sessions} (else the label is omitted with the reason); the spread between them unsigned, ranked the same way; top third of the spread = a lead
labels.source: Schwab 1-min bars via market_context.py, saved by the context job to state/spx_jev/context/{day}.jsonl (live) and state/spx_jev/context/bars/{day}.jsonl (backfill: python -m spx_jev.market_context --backfill 2026-08-10); the symbol must be in market_context.SYMBOLS (QQQ, IWM, SPY)

labels.name: levels.break_armed
labels.example: a break upward is armed: 14 minutes ago price was turned back 0.12 sigma below yesterday's close while the book leaned to puts; it expires in 31 minutes if price does not close through that level
labels.computed_how: level_reclaim.break_state, cock_direction, cock_level_kind (named), distance in sigma, cock_age_min vs 45

labels.name: levels.open_vs_prior_range
labels.example: the settled open is 0.12 sigma above yesterday's high of the day, past the 0.03 sigma buffer; yesterday's range was 0.41 sigma
labels.computed_how: settled open (09:34 close) against yesterday's high/low with the outside_buffer_sigma verdict; the ES-implied 09:25 form waits for the premarket lane

labels.name: levels.prior_day
labels.example: price crossed above yesterday's high 31 minutes ago and has stayed above it for 31 finished minutes, at or past the 20-minute acceptance time; it now sits 0.06 sigma above it, beyond the 0.05 sigma reach
labels.computed_how: prior-day high/low from yesterday's bars; minutes beyond; current location first

labels.name: levels.prior_value
labels.example: price is 0.18 sigma below the low of yesterday's value area (the band where SPX spent 70% of yesterday's session, 0.24 sigma wide), beyond the 0.02 sigma edge distance; yesterday's busiest level is 0.31 sigma above price
labels.computed_how: time-at-price profile from yesterday's 390 1-minute bars (each bar spread over its high-low), point of control and 70% value area; computed at the open

labels.name: levels.round_number
labels.example: 8 minutes ago price rose through a round 100-point level and now sits 0.04 sigma above it; 20 minutes ago it was 0.09 sigma below
labels.computed_how: live spot vs multiples of 50 points; kind named (50 or 100), never the price

labels.name: levels.wall_touch_effort
labels.example: price tested the put-side heavy strike 12 minutes ago and is now 0.09 sigma back from it, not back by more than the 0.10 sigma touch rule, so it is still touching; SPY volume during the touch was in the top band for those minutes (at or above the 70th percentile)
labels.computed_how: siege box verdict on the last touch within 30 minutes; wall side named; the {wall_touch_sigma} touch rule stays a fixed tolerance (owner rule 2026-09-27, kept with its reason): it says only whether price is still at the strike, and a break past a heavy strike is too rare to give a same-minute history of how far past to rank against

labels.name: liquidity.spy_book_lean
labels.example: over the last 5 minutes pressure at SPY's best prices leaned to buyers, 1.4 times the usual spread of readings
labels.computed_how: lob-flow daemon adds bid_size+ask_size before saving; needs per-minute bid/ask sizes and summed order-flow imbalance persisted

labels.name: liquidity.spy_quote
labels.example: over the last 5 minutes SPY's quoted spread has been 3 cents, wider than on 17 of the last 20 sessions at this minute, top third: wide for this time; the size showing at SPY's best bid and offer combined is in the bottom fifth for 14:00, higher than 2 of the last 20 sessions at this minute
labels.computed_how: lob_flow/agg baseline_rows spread|spy and size|spy (NOT the diary spy_depth block, whose size_z/spread_z are null on all rows); the spread in whole cents ranked against the same minute on up to the last 20 sessions, needing same_clock_min_sessions: 'at the tight tick' under spy_spread_tight, else its third, the top third wide; size ranked the same way, stated as a fifth, never in shares

labels.name: news.intraday_headline
labels.example: a Fed governor said rate cuts are off the table, 4 minutes ago
labels.computed_how: needs a scheduled headline writer (right-eye / Nexus into state)

labels.name: news.morning_brief
labels.example: the 09:00 morning brief leans up 0.3 on a -1 to +1 scale, past the 0.2 direction floor, with confidence 0.45, past the 0.3 confidence floor; this morning's gap was 0.30 sigma up, larger than 10 of the last 19 days' gaps, middle third, a real gap, so the brief leans the way the gap went
labels.computed_how: kind=brief reason=morning entry from learning-{day}.jsonl (never the day file, which a midday redive can overwrite); the gap is gap.size's, |09:34 close - prior_close| in sigma_anchor ranked by gap_open.gap_rank against up to the last {night_rank_count} sessions' gaps (needing same_clock_min_sessions, else omitted with the reason); a real gap is one above the bottom third; code writes the sentence with the direction and confidence floor verdicts

labels.name: open.fresh_extreme
labels.example: in the last 5 minutes price set a new session high, 0.05 sigma above the earlier high from 09:52; it now sits 0.02 sigma below that high, in the top band of today's 0.31 sigma range (past the 75% line); it is above the first-15-minute range, which it first broke at 10:01
labels.computed_how: max/min of the last window's bars vs the session extreme before them; day-range band against range_top_share / range_bottom_share; opening-range break clause (first 15 minutes)

labels.name: open.noise_band
labels.example: price is 0.07 sigma above the higher of the settled open and yesterday's close, a stretch bigger than 15 of the last 20 sessions had moved from their settled open by this minute, top third: above the usual move-from-the-open band for 11:30
labels.computed_how: Zarattini-Aziz-Barbon band, ranked: the band is laid above the higher and below the lower of the settled open (09:34 close) and yesterday's close; how far price has stretched past the nearer of the two, as a share of it (0 between them), ranked against how far each prior session had moved from its own settled open by this clock minute, |close / settled open - 1|, on up to the last {night_rank_count} sessions (a session whose morning ruler was estimated sits out; a tie is not beaten), said as 'bigger than N of the last M sessions had moved' and its third, bottom inside / middle at the edge of / top above or below the band; between the two, 'stretched past neither: inside' with the distance to each in sigma; omitted under {same_clock_min_sessions} sessions with the rank's reason

labels.name: open.path
labels.example: 20 minutes after the settled open, price reached 0.22 sigma above it and 0.04 sigma below it, crossed it once, and gave back 18% of its high, under the stall line; price is now 1.6 tape units above the settled open (one tape unit = the typical 5-minute swing right now, 0.11 sigma), more than one tape unit away on the up side, on the gap's side
labels.computed_how: settled open = 09:34 close; high/low since, giveback share against giveback_third ('under / at or past the stall line'), where price sits now in today's tape unit (rulers.ruler: the median high-low range of the last three finished 5-minute slices, floored at ruler_floor_sigma, in the morning anchor): more than one unit either side is away, within one (inclusive) rotating; gap-side clause (on / against the gap's side, or 'with no real gap this morning' when the gap ranks in the bottom third of the last {night_rank_count} sessions' gaps; left out while the gap has no rank); omitted while the unit is held (before 09:45) or the bars have stopped

labels.name: open.settled_open_crosses
labels.example: price sits 0.01 sigma above the settled open; since it was set 25 minutes ago price has crossed it 6 times, more often than 17 of the last 20 sessions had by this minute, top third: contested
labels.computed_how: where price sits against the settled open (09:34 close) first; then the count of 1-minute closes since 09:35 switching side of it (a close on it keeps its side), ranked against the same count from each prior session's own settled open to this clock minute on up to the last {night_rank_count} sessions (every session with bars counts: a count is not in sigma, so an estimated ruler does not leave a day out; a tie is not beaten), said as 'more often than N of the last M sessions had by this minute' and its third, bottom one-sided / middle some crossing / top contested ('no more often than any' when it beats none); omitted under {same_clock_min_sessions} sessions with the rank's reason

labels.name: options.big_prints_10
labels.example: over the last 10 minutes 24 single near-price 0DTE trades of 43 lots or more printed, the largest 0.1% of single trades in these minutes on the last 19 sessions, at least the 5-trade minimum; 21% of their premium whose side could be told was calls bought or puts sold, higher than 3 of the last 18 sessions at this minute, bottom third: a bearish lean
labels.computed_how: lob_flow tape, SORTED by ts_ms (23% of prints arrive out of order), aggressor side from quote at print; a large trade is a single trade at or above the size big_print_pct of the same 10 minutes' single trades stayed at or under, pooled over up to the last 20 sessions' tapes (at least same_clock_min_sessions); the large trades' bullish premium share ranked against the same share on the prior sessions with big_min_prints or more of them, in thirds

labels.name: options.call_put_shift_10m
